notes.about: Odia, in a script the engine has no rules of its own for: this file is all it knows. Sources: data/manifests/orwiki.json, orwikisource.json, aksharantar-ori.json.
notes.notWord: The digits ୦-୯, the isshar sign ୰ and the fraction signs.
notes.firstLetter: Independent vowels, consonants, ଡ଼ ଢ଼ ୟ (U+0B5C-0B5F), ୠ ୡ and the letter ୱ (wa). Never a sign, the anusvara (ଂ), candrabindu or visarga.
notes.signs: Vowel signs, the virama and the length marks must follow a consonant. ଂ ଁ ଃ are left out: they can follow an independent vowel (ଅଂଶ). The nukta is a base, as in Bengali, so a vowel sign may follow ଡ଼ (ଡ + ଼ after NFC: U+0B5C and 0B5D are composition exclusions).
notes.letters: ୟ (U+0B5F, yya) is its own letter and has no decomposition, unlike Bengali's য়; ଯ + nukta, a mis-typing of it, is mended to ୟ. ୱ (U+0B71) is the wa of the -wa sign (ସ୍ୱ).
notes.replace: ଅ + ା typed for ଆ is mended. The two-part vowel signs (େ + ା, େ + ୖ, େ + ୗ) are ୋ ୈ ୌ by NFC, which the normal form already applies. Every ZWJ and ZWNJ is dropped (no joiners field).
notes.phraseBreaks: Odia ends a sentence with the danda । (U+0964); ॥ ends verse.
notes.apostrophe: Odia marks a dropped vowel with an apostrophe inside a word: କ'ଣ (what), ତା'ର (his, for ତାହାର), ତା'ପରେ, ମା'ଙ୍କ. Without it these common words were the top of the dropped list (ତା'ର 1,390 times, କ'ଣ 1,106).
